raw_evidence.quote:
PNG exports work by [Playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) spinning up a headless browser, putting the SVG onto it, and taking a screenshot. The first invocation of Playwright will download its dependencies, if they don't already exist on the machine.

If you get a message like `err: failed to launch Chromium`, you can try installing Playwright dependencies outside of D2 on your machine.
PDF exports are the result of taking PNG exports and placing them on PDF pages, along with headers and fonts. As such, dependencies needed for PNG exports are also needed for PDF.

Does D2 need a browser to run?

No, D2 can run entirely server-side.
A "Layer" represents "a layer of abstraction". Each Layer starts off as a blank board, since you're representing different objects at every level of abstraction.

A "Scenario" represents a different view of the base Layer.

Each Scenario inherits from its base Layer. Any new objects are added onto all objects in the base Layer, and you can reference any objects from the base Layer to update them.

A "Step" represents a step in a sequence of events.

Each Step inherits from its the Step before it. The first step inherits from its parent, whether that's a Scenario or Layer.

named_subset_views_over_one_model.citation: docs/tour/layers.md line 4-5, scenarios.md line 5-8, steps.md line 5-8
named_subset_views_over_one_model.rationale: D2 does provide three composition mechanisms (Layers, Scenarios, Steps) that produce multiple named 'boards' from one .d2 source file, which is a genuine strength worth recording. But their documented purpose differs materially from Structurizr's named views: a Layer starts as a BLANK board representing 'a different level of abstraction' — it does not automatically inherit or subset the base model's shapes, so showing a readable slice of one large model (e.g. just the TASK_INSTANCE/FOLDER_RUN/PLAN tables out of 25 entities) would require manually re-declaring or re-referencing the relevant shapes inside that Layer, not selecting a named subset of the existing model the way a Structurizr view does. Scenarios and Steps DO inherit from a base Layer, so they are closer to overlays than to subset selection — a Scenario shows the base plus/minus explicit modifications, not a chosen subset. None of the three primitives is documented as 'pick N of M existing shapes and render just those' — achieving a 25-entity model split into readable focused sub-diagrams would require restructuring the model into multiple Layers with duplicated or re-referenced shape declarations, which is a workaround, not a first-class subset-view mechanism.

png_export_dependency.rationale: SVG export is native and dependency-free (the CLI's default output format, produced by D2's own renderer). PNG (and PDF/PPTX, which are built from PNG) export is NOT native — it depends on Playwright spinning up a headless Chromium browser, and 'the first invocation of Playwright will download its dependencies, if they don't already exist on the machine.' This has a direct, material consequence for the zero-local-install requirement: whether an official Docker image bundles Playwright/Chromium pre-installed (making PNG export genuinely zero-install inside the container) versus triggering an on-the-fly download at first PNG-export time was NOT confirmed by any source consulted — no Dockerfile or image-contents documentation was found describing this. Recorded as an open gap: SVG export is a clean, dependency-free capability; PNG export carries a headless-browser dependency whose packaging inside the official Docker image is undocumented and unverified.

application_type_generation.citation: GitHub issue-tracker search (repo:d2lang/d2, terms pydantic/sqlalchemy/dataclass/generate types) — zero results
application_type_generation.rationale: D2 is a diagram scripting language with no documented code-generation target of any kind, consistent with its purpose (visual diagramming, not schema authoring). No documentation page under docs/tour/ mentions Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, dataclasses, or any application-type generator, and an issue-tracker search for these terms returned zero results — not even a feature request. Recorded as a definite negative rather than an evidence gap: the absence is corroborated by both silence in official docs and silence in the issue tracker.

ddl_derivation.citation: GitHub issue-tracker search (repo:d2lang/d2, term DDL) — zero results; consistent with application_type_generation finding above
ddl_derivation.rationale: Per the brief's own instruction, DDL derivation is recorded as not-applicable rather than not-expressible because no type-generation pipeline exists in D2 to derive DDL from in the first place — there is nothing for a DDL-derivation feature to sit on top of. The issue-tracker search for 'DDL' returned zero results, consistent with this never having been requested or discussed.

contrary_evidence_search.result: No documentation page or issue mentions application-type generation or DDL derivation in any form — a clean, corroborated negative. No documentation page explicitly frames Layers/Scenarios/Steps as answering a 'named subset view of one large model' need; the closest framing found is 'a layer of abstraction' (layers.md) and 'a different view of the base Layer' (scenarios.md), which describe overlay/abstraction-level semantics rather than subset selection — recorded as a workaround-level match to the survey's named-subset-view question, not a clean match.
